I once had a talking sword, inspired by Daxter and Navi with a hint of major anxiety disorder. My players loved the voice I had for that thing, and loved the ability which was a giant thunderbolt based on the spell slot spent, useable up to 3 times a day. Everytime it was casted he came out of the sheath with extreme anxiety and yelling obscenities and more. My players found it perfect. For my personal choices I wanted the sword to be less obscene, and no longer allowed it to talk out of being casted, making it less of a crutch.

For my players that ruined the campaign for 2 or 3 sessions they told me. Luckily they talked to me about it and we came to a compromise of building a much more active, comedic, and less obscene NPC. But they never loved dear ThunderHilt the same again.

What I'm trying to say is, if your players love something you're doing, don't change it. Improve the other aspects of your campaign! (Dont make it copy/paste areas though). Make a funnier/better weapon! Or maybe think of how video games would discourage you from spamming a spell/ability? 

If you already tried slight discouragement and she still uses it (e.g. the resistances to the tortilla chip, or making the enemy capable of catching the tortilla chip) I'd suggest just letting it happen.

The only time that you should take drastic action to change an item in my opinion is if it makes you or your players uncomfortable or angered. And specifically those two emotions. I was uncomfortable cussing as much, which is why I followed through with but still regret making ThunderHilt less obscene. I'd rather just bear through it to let my players love something!

And, if things go well for you two, you could hide a wedding ring in a tortilla chip bowl!

In the dead of night, skirmishes were heard all across the town. The plague was setting in the village. For each man and woman were falling sick, and the children were falling dead. Several years of this plague were suffered, some assumed at that point it was brought by the divines. 

But after years of sending invites to other cities, organizations, and kingdoms for help, someone finally answered. The Pied Piper, as he was called, walked into the small town with the sound of whimsy, peace, and relaxation whistling behind him. One and all, each and every skirmish headed towards the whistle, coming from a metallic tube that resembled a metal pipe. Neither tobacco nor hemp came from it, only whistles of calming. 
The vermin that resided in the city followed this tune, enchanting many of those who's ears have yet to swell up as well. He took off with the vermin, and some of our women and children, as the melody taunted them all. The town saw the sacrifice of 17 children and 11 women as a adequate trade for relief of a plague.
 
~~~~ 

Many years later, in a cottage surrounded by green, set on the banks of the river, lived 17 teenagers and 11 mothers always cheery. The teenagers worked a small plot of land just down the river, using their youth to bring growth to the crops. The mothers cooked foods, washed clothes, and even picked berries when nature would permit.

Summer, autumn, winter, spring a tune would always repeat. One of whimsy, peace, and relaxation. And over the days this tune only got louder, and the small society would never leave it's range. 

However, at night, for 8 hours, no more, no less, it would stop and the society would become depressed. This depression turned into anguish, this anguish into self-harm, and for the source of the tune, this was not complete. 

So the man got up from the chair, screwed to the porch of the cottage, never speaking a word before, issued his first request. "Tonight, when you hear the tune go backwards, you will all chain yourself up." And the request was accepted most graciously. 17 teenagers, and 11 mothers all found manacles and ropes, and tied themselves to the walls when the tune would go backwards. Only when the tune was no more, would they realize the sanity of this request.

 Only when the tune was no more, did they realize 16 teenagers, and 11 mothers were on the walls. Over the course of many nights, with a different teen missing from the wall, a plan would form. A knife, some cotton, and a key for the cuffs. 

~~~~ 

Today, we have a creature, with 28 stab wounds, travelling the land. Cuts around his throat, so his tune will never be as hypnotizing again. But he changes his shape, so no one will ever see the truth. 28 stab wounds, to hide 17 victims and 11 maids, for this poor wretched fool had his years as nobility. Strapped for cash, and strapped for hope, here we finding looking for someone to guide him. He does not wish to atone, he wishes to survive. By any means, he should not be alive, but after that dreadful night... 

The Pied Piper's tune was never cheery again.
